# Praelecta

> AI lecture recording and study tool for university students. Record the lecture; by the time you are out of the room it is a transcript, a summary, flashcards and practice questions. Tick which lectures a test covers, and the study sessions book themselves around your calendar. Made in Canada, priced in CAD, billed by the semester.

Praelecta is built for undergraduate students in content-heavy courses (engineering, sciences, math) who would rather not redo the whole course at exam time. It is a web app (praelecta.ca) with desktop apps for Mac, Windows and Linux; an iPhone app is on the way.

What it does:
- Records a lecture (up to six hours) after the student confirms they have permission, then transcribes it (Groq; Deepgram as a fallback) and writes the summary, key concepts, formulas, definitions, worked examples, exam mentions and to-dos (Google Gemini).
- Attaches the professor's files (slides, syllabus, formula sheets, past exams) to a lecture or a course; formulas are verified against them, and practice material can be built from them.
- Lets the student tick which lectures a test covers, so flashcards, practice questions, quizzes and class handbooks stay inside that slice.
- Books study sessions between now and the exam around the student's classes and work shifts, rebooks missed ones, and runs a focus timer with an end-of-session review.
- Imports a class timetable from a photo or PDF to set up the semester.

Pricing (CAD): two full lectures free with no card. Student $7.99/month or $24.99/semester (200 credits a month, about 20 recorded lectures); Scholar $12.99/month or $39.99/semester (450 credits); Unlimited $24.99/month or $79.99/semester (1000 credits). A one-hour lecture costs 10 credits. Credit packs (100 for $6.99, 250 for $14.99, 500 for $27.99) never expire. Cancel in one tap; the price you sign up at never rises while you stay subscribed.

Commitments: a recording never cuts out mid-lecture; every limit is visible before you hit it; cancelling is one tap; the app helps with lectures, never with writing assignments. Recordings are private to the student's account and are deleted when they delete them.
